Subject: On-prem crypto profile and BYO key rotation — initial questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for walking us through the deployment options last week. As we start the on-prem onboarding planning, our security team asked for a short list of clarifications around BYOK + HSM integration for the private/VPC deployment. Attached is a simple spreadsheet (BYOK_requirements.xlsx) with the fields they want populated. High level items they care about:

- Operator separation and how Redwood limits human access to the HSM key material.
- Rotation window and whether Redwood supports automated rolling of wrapped keys vs. manual rotate-on-demand.
- Attestation & logs: what proofs we can provide for a cutover and periodic audits (hashes, attestations).
- Network topology: where the HSM/control-plane endpoints are reachable from customer subnets, and if customers must allow egress to Redwood control plane.

Can you and your ops/security contacts fill in the spreadsheet or reply with guidance? We aim to complete our security sign-off within two weeks.

Thanks,

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Villalobos <maria@orchid-systems.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem crypto profile and BYO key rotation — initial questions

Hi Maria — thank you, this is helpful. Looping in Sofia (security lead for Private) and Ben (onprem ops) so we can be explicit in the spreadsheet. Below are direct answers to each of the bullets; we will also populate the XLSX and upload the HSM network diagram.

Operator separation / human access
- Redwood supports split-operator custody for customer BYOK: the default is a 2-of-3 threshold for unseal operations, configurable to higher thresholds. Customer retains control of the key material; Redwood never holds unwrapped customer keys for hosted Private deployments.
- We provide a role-based operator flow: operators are distinct identities (HSM operator, Escrow officer, Auditor). We recommend at least two offsite operators for production keys.

Rotation model
- We support both automated scheduled rotations (API-driven wrap/rotate) and manual rotates initiated by the customer. For production, we recommend quarterly cryptographic rotations with monthly ephemeral rewrap for session keys.
- When automation is enabled, Redwood performs a zero-downtime rewrap where active KV cache entries are re-associated with the new wrapped key according to the rollout window in the rotation policy.

Attestation & logs
- HSM attestation (quote) for each wrap/unwrap event is captured and logged. We provide signed attestations (platform key) and a delivery of audit bundles on request (S3 presigned link or direct upload to your SIEM).
- Audit logs include operator identity, IP (customer egress point), operation type, and attestation nonce. We can produce a tamper-evident bundle for audits.

Network topology & endpoints
- For on-prem deployment we place an HSM gateway in your VPC that speaks only over your private subnet to Redwood Private control-plane endpoints. The HSM gateway requires outbound TLS to: control.redwood-inference.com:443 (mutual TLS) for control signals and to attestation.redwood-inference.com:9443 for attestation verification.
- You can also run an air-gapped HSM; in that case attestations are collected via signed bundles and ingested through a signed-ticket workflow (no direct egress required).

I attached the HSM network diagram and a short markdown with the rotation schedule we recommend. If that looks good, Ben and I can complete the spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.

– Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: On-prem crypto profile and BYO key rotation — initial questions

Thanks — quick operational notes / clarifications from ops perspective:

- Dual-threshold recommendation: for Orchid we suggest a 3-of-5 operator model for production HSM unseals where two of the five operators are customer-controlled, and three are escrowed customer-admins (distributed across two sites). This reduces blast radius.

- Ephemeral wrapping for session tokens: Redwood issues ephemeral wrapping keys per workload instance with TTLs (default 24h). Recommended pattern: long-lived master wrapped key (BYOK) + short-lived wrapping keys for runtime session tokens. In practice this means that a compromise of a node reveals only current session tokens (limited TTL) and not the master key.

- Key rotation playbook (summary):
  1) Stage new wrapped key in HSM gateway (wrap with customer public material).
  2) Start sombra rewrap pass (shadow write) for new key while reads still point at old key.
  3) Switch reads over during low-traffic window (we provide a canary switch).
  4) Retire old key after retention window (recommend 30d for rollback).

- Egress minimization: if you prefer no outbound to our control plane, we can run a signed-bundle ingestion mode (you'll push attestations/log bundles via secure SFTP to our intake pipeline). This increases cutover friction but preserves strict egress constraints.

I pasted the short snippet from our rotation automation to illustrate the API call we use (replace placeholders):

POST /v1/private/keys/rotate
Authorization: Bearer <operator-token>
{
  "key_id": "orchid-master-2027",
  "policy": {
    "rollout_window": "PT2H",
    "canary_percent": 5,
    "retention_days": 30
  }
}

Happy to run a short tabletop with your SecOps team on Friday if useful.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Onprem Engineer — Redwood Inference
